title: Paul’s command to prove whether Christ is in us implies discernible marks of living faith
source_text: XI. Similiter, nisi ex signis certis & indubitatis dignoscere possemus, an Christus per fidem veram & vivam in nobis habitet, frustra jubet Paulus ut nos ipsos probaremus & excuteremus, An Christus sit in nobis, & an simus in fide. 2 Cor. 13. Unde colligitur fideles ex signis evidentibus dignoscere posse, an sint fide in Christum praediti; Christumque fidelibus inhabitantem sui sensum non obscurum illis praebere.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise, unless we could distinguish by certain and undoubted signs whether Christ dwells in us by true and living faith, Paul would in vain command that we prove and examine ourselves whether Christ is in us and whether we are in the faith (2 Cor. 13). From which it is gathered that believers can distinguish by evident signs whether they are endowed with faith in Christ; and that Christ dwelling in believers affords them a sense of himself that is not obscure.
pass_b_english: Self-examination would be pointless if living faith had no certain marks.
Christ’s indwelling yields a sense of himself clear enough for believers to read.
